To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
limnological factors influence Cd bioaccumulation and MT synthesis in freshwater bivaves, but the relative contribution of these factors is small compared with that of the Cd exposure gradient.

(1) limnological factors influence Cd bioaccumulation and MT synthesis in freshwater benthic organisms; (2) the relative influence of limnplogical factors on Cd bioaccumulation in benthic organisms is lower than that of free Cd2+; (3) the relative influence on MT synthesis in benthic invertebrates is similar to that on Cd bioaccumlation; (4) limnological confounders can be minimized in the selection of lakes to monitor Cd
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relative influence of the limnological variability and the exposure gradient of the contaminant on the accumulation of the contaminant and the synthesis of the biomarker of effect in natural populations of organisms.
the influence of limnology on the bioaccumulation of Cd and MT synthesis in freshwater bialves living in lakes.
the influence of environmental factors on metal bioaccumulation and MT synthesis in aquatic organisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

limnological factors do not explain the entire variation in Cd and metallothioneins concentrations in the gill tissues of freshwater bivalve Pyganodon grandis, but that they are important and must be considered when assessing the relative influence of the Cd exposure gradient versus the limnological variability on the metal bioaccumulation and MT synthesis.
the limnology of a water body is a key factor that must be considered when interpreting bioaccumulation data in freshwater organisms.
the influence of the metal gradient was more important than the influence of the limnological variability on Cd accumulation in the bivalves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cd bioaccumulation and MT synthesis in bivalves is mainly controlled by limnological factors, which should be considered in the interpretation of biomonitoring results.

the relative influence of the environmental variables was lower than expected, which may be due to the fact that we were able to measure the most important limnological factors that influence the bioaccumulation of Cd and MT synthesis.

the limnology of the lakes where the bivalves are sampled has to be taken into account in order to interpret the results of biomonitoring programs based on the analysis of metal concentrations and/or MT concentrations in the tissues of bivalves.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the relative importance of the environmental variables that are likely to affect metal bioavailability varies depending on the metal and the biological compartment considered, which has important implications for the interpretation of bioaccumulation data.

the relative influence of limno-chemical variables on Cd bioaccumulation and MT synthesis in bivalves can be estimated using a multiple linear regression model that includes the total concentration of Cd in the water compartment as an explanatory variable.

the relative influence of limno-chemical confounding variables on the metal exposure gradient is important, and that the use of a selection procedure to minimise the influence of these factors is recommended for the design of monitoring programs in metal-polluted environments.
